subject: Clarify: regional routing, subprocessors, and data transfer for Medidata POC
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medidata-health.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medidata-health.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial Qs on where PII will be processed for POC

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team was impressed with the latency profile. As we scope the POC, the security team asked for a short Q&A focused on where data will be processed and what subprocessors may touch it. High-level Qs below:

1) For the hosted POC, which physical regions could customer data be processed in (primary + fallbacks)?
2) If we pin to a US-only processing policy, do you have a list of subprocessors that still might see any data (s3 storage, monitoring, observability)?
3) Are there any automatic cross-border routing behaviors (e.g., failover to eu region) we should be aware of?
4) For deletion requests, what is the SLA and which components retain cached prefixes / KV cache after deletion?

Appreciate concise answers we can share with InfoSec. If easier, feel free to share a short inventory or a diagram.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Security Programs, Medidata Health
security@medidata-health.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medidata-health.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial Qs on where PII will be processed for POC

Laura — thanks for the clear list. I'll loop in Aditya (infra lead) and Marissa (security/controls) and we can reply with a short inventory + diagram. Quick answers in-line below and we'll follow up with the attachments you can share with InfoSec.

1) Regions: primary routing for hosted customers is "us-west-2" (Oregon) by default for US accounts. We have regional fallbacks configured (us-east-1) and explicit EU routes (eu-west-1) if a customer requests EU residency.

2) Subprocessors: core GPU serving runs on our Dedicated clusters (proprietary runtime). Supporting services that may process or store transient artifacts include: customer S3 (backup/ingress), Datadog (metrics/traces), and our encrypted logging store (AWS KMS-backed). We'll provide an inventory CSV.

3) Cross-border routing: automatic failover does NOT cross geopolitical boundaries for accounts flagged as "EU-only" or "US-only"; for non-restricted accounts, failover may route to the nearest healthy region based on latency and capacity. We can pin the POC to US-only to avoid that.

4) Deletion SLA: we offer a 30-day retention window for user-requested content in the hosted plan; deletion propagation to caches (KV/prefix) is targeted within 24 hours for primary caches and up to 72 hours for multi-layered cold artifacts. For POCs we can accelerate to 7 days with a written agreement.

I'll attach the region map and a subprocessor inventory in the next email.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Thanks Jonas — that helps. Two clarifying items from our side:

• For the "supporting services" you listed (Datadog, encrypted logging store), can you confirm whether any plaintext customer payloads or prompts are included in those artifacts or are they strictly telemetry/metadata?

• For the 30-day default deletion window, does that apply to model inputs (prompts), generated outputs, and embeddings equally? Our compliance team prefers explicit per-artifact SLAs.

If you can add a simple mapping table in the inventory (artifact -> retention SLA -> encryption at rest), that would be ideal.

Best,
Laura

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medidata-health.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial Qs on where PII will be processed for POC

Laura — attaching the inventory and a regional transfer diagram per your request (see attachments). Key points summarized below for InfoSec: 

- Supporting services and telemetry: We do not persist plaintext customer prompts to third-party telemetry providers. Datadog receives only anonymized metrics/traces (no prompt content). Our encrypted logging store receives structured request/response hashes and system logs; full payloads are only stored in customer-configured object storage (S3) when the customer enables backups.

- Retention mapping (summary):
  * Model inputs (prompts): default 30 days retention for hosted; can be configured down to 7 days for POC (flagged in account settings).
  * Generated outputs: default 30 days, configurable; ephemeral streaming responses are not persisted unless configured.
  * Embeddings: treated as derived artifacts; default 90 days unless customer opts into long-term vector store export.

- Cross-border behavior: For the POC we'll set the tenancy to US-only. That enforces region pins and disables cross-region fallback for this account. If you later request geo-failover, we'll provide a documented change with timelines.

- Deletion propagation: 24h for hot caches (KV/prefix), 72h for warm/cold artifacts; explicit immediate purge requests require a data-escrow workflow and are handled as a paid compliance action (we've done this for several clinical customers).

Attachments included: redwood-region-map.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-2027-07.csv, transfer-flow-diagram.png

If InfoSec wants, Marissa can join a 30-min call to walk through the CSV and the encryption/traceability controls. Would Wed or Thu next week work?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
